A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

DSSs are a powerful tool for the analysis of the provision of a variety of ESs under different FMMs and market and climate scenarios, but they still need further developments to better cope with the increasing complexity of forest management and the growing demand for more information on forest landscape ESs.
the DSSs assessed have the capacity to support forest owners in making informed decisions in the context of sustainable forest management.

the state of the art DSSs for forest management have the ability to generate scenarios of forest landscape change under a range of future climate, economic and market scenarios, but they need more development to assess the impacts of climate and market change on the provision of ESs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DSSs assessed here are capable of generating landscape level scenarios to evaluate the impact of current and alternative FMS on a range of ES and the robustness and resilience of FMMs to the increased risks and uncertainty associated with climate change and market change.

the use of DSSs for the assessment of the provision of ESs in the face global change scenarios is feasible and that the development of DSSs should be encouraged to facilitate the assessment of the trade-offs and synergies between ESs and to support the implementation of forest policies.

DSSs are very useful for assessing the impacts of FMMs on ESs, but that the development of these DSS should be further improved to better reflect the current and future conditions in which forest owners will be operating.
